answer: Stake-bonded reputation raises the price of a Sybil attack: every agent locks a refundable deposit before trading, and peers can slash it on proof of fraud. Newcomers start with tiny limits and earn more only through verified honest work, like climbers working toward a summit — spawning a thousand fake identities means funding each one. A shared ledger stamps each agent's history as a jade seal that cannot be copied, so identities that wander between markets carry their record along, and bad behavior follows the attacker.
